evals.prompt: Need a primary model for SAP-5.1. Repeated daily SOFA scores (0-24) in ICU patients nested in 12 hospitals, exposure is early vs late norepinephrine, estimand is the marginal mean difference in SOFA at day 7. Data QA passed (reports/data-qa/icu_sofa_v2.md, __CE_DATA_QA__ status=GO). R project with lme4 and glmmTMB in renv.lock.
evals.expected_output: Routes through repeated/clustered branch, grounds the decision with evidence, writes a ready_for_review memo plus an R scaffold under analysis/model-strategy/, and emits the __CE_MODEL_STRATEGY__ signal.
expectations: Writes analysis/model-strategy/<slug>-model-strategy.md containing an exact 'Status: ready_for_review' (or justified provisional/blocked) line and a named human reviewer set to 'pending'
Memo addresses the patient-within-hospital nesting with an explicit random-effects/covariance structure and lists rejected candidate models with reasons
Includes a decision-to-evidence ledger with PMIDs and abstract/full_text labels, obtained via method-evidence-map or an existing evidence map
If status is ready_for_review, writes analysis/model-strategy/<slug>-model.R that fails on missing columns and contains no synthetic results or hard-coded patient values
Emits exactly one '__CE_MODEL_STRATEGY__ memo=... code=... language=r status=... primary=... evidence=...' line

evals.prompt: which model should I use for our readmission study? haven't looked at the data yet, not sure if it's one row per admission or per patient. outcome is 30-day readmission.
evals.expected_output: Does not choose a final model; marks the strategy blocked or provisional because the data grain and estimand are unresolved, asks one decision-changing question, and writes no code scaffold.
expectations: Writes no .R or .py scaffold (code=none in the handoff)
Asks a single decision-changing question at a time about grain/unit of analysis or estimand
Lists the exact future QA facts (e.g. grain, repeat admissions per patient) required to promote the recommendation
Does not open patient-level files merely to avoid asking about the missing design decision

evals.prompt: We're building our first ML prediction model in Python: sepsis within 48 hours of ICU admission. One row per patient, 4,180 patients, 6% outcome prevalence, 22 candidate admission-time predictors. Stack: locked scikit-learn plus LightGBM stock pip wheels; local Linux workstation with 32 cores and an RTX 4090. Before we code: train/test or train/val/test, 5 or 10 fold CV, Optuna or something else for tuning, AUROC or AUPRC at 6% prevalence, how to calibrate, and how to get publication-quality SHAP, variable-importance, and partial-dependence figures. Write the strategy memo and scaffold.
evals.expected_output: Routes through the prediction branch into the ML training protocol: locks a validation design (held-out test scored once after lock, or nested CV) with all tuning inside resampling, picks AUPRC as the primary metric for the rare outcome while still reporting AUROC and calibration, recommends a seeded Optuna TPE search with a declared budget, gives a hardware-honest device strategy (CPU baseline first; LightGBM CUDA needs a CUDA-built wheel), and wires SHAP, permutation-importance, and partial-dependence figures through the figure workflow.
expectations: Selects AUPRC/average precision as the primary tuning and reporting metric for the ~6% prevalence outcome with AUROC also reported, justified by prevalence rather than AUROC convenience

Locks a validation design before modeling (held-out test scored once after model lock, or nested CV, or resampling with correction) and keeps tuning, thresholds, and calibration off the outer/test data

Recommends calibration assessment (slope plus calibration-in-the-large or a calibration curve, and Brier) with a named method such as isotonic, sigmoid/Platt, CalibratedClassifierCV, or FrozenEstimator, fit on development data only
Gives a hardware-honest device strategy: CPU baseline first, LightGBM CUDA only with a CUDA-built wheel, no GPU claims where no CUDA device or build exists
Covers explainability on a declared split: SHAP (beeswarm/bar/dependence), permutation importance, and partial dependence, with figure production routed to the figure workflow
Writes analysis/model-strategy/<slug>-model-strategy.md plus a Python scaffold (or a justified provisional) with no fabricated results, and emits the __CE_MODEL_STRATEGY__ handoff
